I wish I could offer some help or advice, but I have 0 experience with Surface. I'm not here to shitpost, so I do have one piece of general advice. Linux, or any new operating system you're diving into, requires patience and learning. When I started with Linux about a decade ago I was getting desperate every hour of using it, and believe me the situation then was much worse than it is now when it comes to software and driver support. Dozens of times I was on the brink of declaring it absolute shit and going back to Windows, but I kept learning and fixing issues only because I was stubborn enough and because I couldn't get my printer to work on Windows anymore while the Linux drivers for that HP was probably the only functional thing. Fast forward to now and all of my machines are running Linux in some shape of form, Gentoo, Arch, Slackware, Manjaro.

Previous poster suggested you try Manjaro, and I agree with that. It's good for beginners and intermediate users but it will require your attention more often than Ubuntu because it's based on Arch, meaning it's a rolling release distro.
